To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sorption of the herbicides alachlor, amitrol, atrazine, imazamex, imazethaphyr, pendimethalin, simazine, and dicamba to soils from the Baltic region is affected by the soil properties of pH, soil organic carbon content, and soil texture, but not by cation exchange capacity.

the measured sorption coefficients of the eight herbicides to seven agricultural soils in Lithuania follow the general trend pendemethalin > alcholr > atrazine ∼ amitrole ∼ simazine > izamethapyr > izamox > dicambe.

the sorption coefficients of several commonly used herbicides to agricultural soils from Lithuania follow the trend pendimethaline > alachlor ∼ atrazine ∼ amitrole ∼ simazine >imazethapyr ∼ imazamox ∼ dicamba, consistent in general with the trend in hydrophobicities (log Kow).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the analysis of the sorption and mobility of the herbicides in the Baltic region soils.
the sorption of pesticides in Baltic soils and the potential of pesticides to contaminate ground and surface waters.
the development of a new method for the determination of the sorption coefficients of pesticides to soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study will be useful in developing a better understanding of pesticide sorption to Lithuanian agricultural soils and in predicting herbicide leaching to groundwater.
herbicides with low Kow values and low organic carbon contents are most likely to be mobile, while those with high Kow values and high organic carbon contents are the least mobile.
the sorption of pesticides in the soils of the Baltic region, in general, is comparable with that of other soils in Europe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
herbicide sorption to soil is important in controlling leaching, but that soil texture is a more important factor in determining leaching rates than herbicide sorption coefficients.
sorption of herbicides to soils is a function of both organic carbon content and soil texture.
sorption of pesticides to soils is a complex process and is influenced by a variety of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil organic matter content is a critical factor affecting the sorption of the herbicides to the soils and thus their mobility in the soils.
the herbicides studied in the Baltic region have different sorption properties in soils.
the herbicides studied in the Baltic region are generally sorbed to soil and are unlikely to leach to the aquifers.
